did.abstract: The Meserve-Kunhardt Collection chiefly consists of photographic material, as well as papers and realia that document the work of Frederick Hill Meserve. A collector and distributor of photographs from 1897 to his death in 1962, Meserve built an extensive collection of material related to Abraham Lincoln as well as other persons, sites, and events of the long nineteenth century. The collection also documents the stewardship and development of the collection from 1962 to 2015 by his descendants, especially his daughter, Dorothy Turner Meserve Kunhardt. The material in the collection provides rich visual documentation of United States history, especially persons, sites, and events during the American Civil War, and details the emergence of photography as a distinctive cultural practice into the early twentieth century.

bioghist.head: History of the Meserve-Kunhardt Collection
bioghist.p: Frederick Hill Meserve (1865-1962) began collecting photographs around 1897-1900 to illustrate the American Civil War memoir of his father, William Neal Meserve (1840-1928) with images of persons and sites mentioned therein. The elder Meserve drafted his narrative during the 1890s; it covers his military service from August 1862 to June 1865, and includes accounts of battles at Antietam (where he reportedly suffered two wounds), Fredericksburg, the Wilderness, and Cold Harbor, as well as engagements outside Petersburg, including the battles at the Crater and Weldon Railroad. A copy of the memoir will become available as other portions of the Collection are processed.

Over a period of sixty years as he amassed an extensive collection of photographs documenting the American Civil War as well as American history and culture over the long nineteenth century, Frederick Hill Meserve became the preeminent collector and historian of photographic images of Abraham Lincoln. He sought to identify and preserve every photograph taken of the sixteenth president.

Meserve privately published many illustrated works, including his the twenty-eight-volume Historical Portraits: A Part of the Collection of Americana of Frederick Hill Meserve, New York City (New York: Privately printed, 1913-1915).

Eventually Meserve's daughter, Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt (1901-1979), joined in his research and collecting efforts. Her son, Philip Bradish Kunhardt, Jr. (1928-2006) continued the project, writing extensively about Lincoln and preserving what became known as the Meserve-Kunhardt Collection at his home in Chappaqua, New York.

In 1981, the National Portrait Gallery acquired its Meserve Collection from the family. That collection includes the "cracked-plate" portrait of Abraham Lincoln by Alexander Gardner and more than 5,400 original negatives from the studio of Mathew B. Brady.

The descendants of Philip Bradish Kunhardt, Jr., including his sons Philip Bradish Kunhardt, III (born 1951), and Peter Whiting Kunhardt, Sr. (born 1952), as well as his grandson, Peter Whiting Kunhardt, Jr. (born 1982), continued to care for the remaining collection. In 2002, they formed the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation, a tax-exempt nonprofit organization dedicated to the preservation of oral and visual history and the use of it to inform, educate, and inspire.

In 2004, the National Endowment for the Humanities awarded the Meserve-Kunhardt Collection a Save America's Treasures grant, declaring that "the collection is an essential tool for Lincoln scholarship and for studying American cities and social movements." With this grant and other funding, the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation sought to preserve the collection and make it available to the public.

In 2007, the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation established a new division, the Gordon Parks Foundation, dedicated to the preservation of creative work by photographer, author, and film director Gordon Parks (1912-2006). The foundation subsequently acquired the archive of another photographer, Ed Clark (1911-2000).

In summer 2009, the collections administered by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation relocated to the State University of New York-Purchase. Shortly before acquisition of the Meserve-Kunhardt Collection by the Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation relocated its collections to Pleasantville, New York. Material related to Gordon Parks and Ed Clark is not part of the collection acquired by the Beinecke.

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: Meserve-Kunhardt Collection. General Collection, Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Yale University.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: This finding aid will be revised as additional parts of the collection are processed and as revisions in arrangement or description are made by staff.

During their stewardship of the collection, the staff of the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation applied "Meserve numbers" (expressed in this guide as a five digit number with the prefix "MES") to photographs in the collection. In doing so, they extended a numbering system established by Frederick Hill Meserve to organize and identify his photographic images. At this point (January 2017), it is not apparent at what number the staff began to apply new numbers. The Foundation also established its own sequence for drafts, galleys, and printed works (expressed as MESB6733-MESB8760). It does not appear that the Foundation used a consistent methodology to assign Meserve numbers; while each Meserve number corresponds to an individual record in a FileMaker Pro database created by the Foundation, the record may describe an individual photograph or a group of related photographs.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Meserve-Kunhardt Collection chiefly consists of photographic material, as well as papers and realia that document the work of Frederick Hill Meserve. A collector and distributor of photographs from 1897 to his death in 1962, Meserve built an extensive collection of material related to Abraham Lincoln as well as other persons, sites, and events of the long nineteenth century. The collection also documents the stewardship and development of the collection from 1962 to 2015 by his descendants, especially his daughter, Dorothy Turner Meserve Kunhardt. The material in the collection provides rich visual documentation of United States history, especially persons, sites, and events during the American Civil War, and details the emergence of photography as a distinctive cultural practice into the early twentieth century.

"Workbooks" represent the first portion of the collection opened for research in January 2017. They consist of copy prints that Meserve made or commissioned between 1897 and 1962 that index original portraiture within the larger collection. The photographs document more than 6,500 individuals on more than ten thousand gelatin silver prints. The images include portraits of Abraham Lincoln and Ulysses S. Grant, as well as military and governmental personnel for the United States and Confederate States of America during the American Civil War. Groups of portraits also document cabinet members in presidential administrations from William Henry Harrison through Woodrow Wilson, as well as statesmen, authors, poets, clergy, actors, actresses, and other entertainers chiefly in the United States, but also from Europe and Asia.

Cased photographs chiefly consists of daguerreotypes, ambrotypes, and tintypes mounted primarily in contemporary decorative cases chiefly collected by Meserve and Kunhardt during the twentieth century. The collection contains 259 entries for individual items or small collections of related material that document photographic processes and presentation techniques primarily in the United States from circa 1845 to circa 1867.

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: The Meserve-Kunhardt Collection is the physical property of the Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Yale University. Literary rights, including copyright, belong to the authors or their legal heirs and assigns. For further information, consult the appropriate curator.

arrangement.p: Series I consists of seven subseries: Workbooks, Cased Photographs, Stereographs and Half Stereographs, Tintypes, Cartes-de-visite and Small Mounted Photographic Prints, Card Photographs and Mounted Photographs, and Unmounted Photographic Prints.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of "workbooks" compiled by Meserve that allowed him to collocate copy prints usually of photographic portraits, but occasionally artwork, with images of named people and provide access chiefly to portraiture within his larger collection. In their early iteration, the workbooks likely informed the publication of his twenty-eight-volume Historical Portraits: A Part of the Collection of Americana of Frederick Hill Meserve, New York City (New York: Privately printed, 1913-1915).

The workbooks consist of 803 heavy paper sheets, 42 x 59 cm, folded in half to form two pages with cut corner mounts to display up to 16 mounted gelatin silver prints, 8.4 x 5.4 cm, on each page, but few pages hold a full 16 images. Groups of sheets were originally stored in deteriorating folders that have been discarded. Each folded sheet is now housed in an individual archival folder.

The 10,485 mounted gelatin silver prints on the sheets document 6,536 discrete subjects. For 672 individuals, Meserve collected sufficient images to require multiple sheets. Meserve occasionally stored sheets devoted to a single individual in different categories. In all cases, individual sheets are now stored in distinct folders following Meserve's original categorization.

Meserve organized the sheets into the nineteen broad categories now used as headings within this guide. Within each category, he positioned prints in a rough alphabetical order by gathering surnames beginning with the same letter on each sheet or sequence of sheets. For portraits of stage women and stage men, the light-colored and dark-colored paper sheets also distinguish discrete groups, which may represent material collected at different times.

This guide provides an alphabetical list of individuals under the categories Meserve assigned them. The list, which does not represent the physical arrangement of the images, provides the box and folder location of images for each named person or place.

Meserve's pages also bear 561 inscriptions below mounts that lacked photographic prints when the Library received the collection. This guide lists these inscriptions followed by the phrase, "No photographic print extant."
Except in a few cases, the list entries do not document the photographer or image creator.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Organized under four headings: Images by Identified Photographers, Identified Subjects by Unidentified Photographers, Unidentified Subjects by Unidentified Photographers, and Cased Photograph Components.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: The processing archivist and Library staff devised form of names and life dates from the Library of Congress Authorities files or original research.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries chiefly consists of daguerreotypes, ambrotypes, and tintypes mounted in contemporary decorative cases primarily collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century. The description contains 259 entries for individual items or small collections of related material that document photographic processes and presentation techniques in the United States from approximately 1845 to approximately 1867.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derive from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Arranged alphabetically by the name of the photographer or firm, and items under each name heading are arranged chronologically.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Balch worked as an itinerant photographer in the American South from 1846-1849, and then operated a gallery in Joliet, Illinois, 1849-1859, and worked again as an itinerant photographer in Kentucky and Tennessee, 1859-1861, as well as operating a galleries in Memphis, Tennessee, 1862-1869, and in Hot Springs, Arkansas, 1872-1879.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: Jenkins was a photographer and inventor. He operated a gallery with James Barrows in Boston, Massachusetts, 1848-1850, and probably operated his own gallery in New York City, circa 1850-1852. In 1851, he registered a United States Patent No. 7,974 for a method of securing daguerreotypes in headstones. In 1852-1853, he worked as an operator employed by Jesse H. Whitehurst in Richmond, Virginia, and in the early 1854 as an operator for I. Tucker in Columbia, South Carolina. In 1854, he opened his own galley in Columbia; He died of yellow fever on November 17, 1854.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: North worked as a photographer in Boston, Massachusetts, 1848-1849, and in Rondout, New York in 1850. In October 1850, he opened a gallery in Cleveland, Ohio, and continued to operate galleries until 1860. North is often confused with his nephew and fellow photographer, Walter Crane North (1831-1891).

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This group of material consists of items involved in the construction of cased photographs. It is comprised primarily of cases, case covers, and case bottoms, as well as examples of preservers, a mat, and a backing plate. Some of the case covers were formerly mismatched to cased photographs in the Meserve-Kunhardt Collection.

did.physdesc: 9 boxes

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries chiefly consists of stereographs and half stereographs primarily collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.

Stereographs present stereoscopic photographs, which are double photographs of the same image taken from two slightly different perspectives with twin-lens cameras, creating a three-dimensional effect when viewed through a stereoscope. The description contains 805 entries for stereographs, which includes 18 double sided stereographs, which also include 17 duplicate stereographs.

Half stereographs are photographs originally taken as one of a pair of stereoscopic photographs but then printed or mounted as a single image. The bulk of the half stereographs in this group were created from full examples of stereographs. The description contains 92 entries for half stereographs.

Images created during the nineteenth century and well-documented in this subseries include views of New York City as well as sites and events related to the American Civil War including views at the battlefield at Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, and parades at Washington, D.C., following the conclusion of the war. Many of the stereographs related to the conflict were published decades later.

Images created during the twentieth century and well-documented in this subseries include images related to William McKinley and his presidential administration as well as the presidential administration and domestic travel of Theodore Roosevelt.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derive from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Organized under three headings: Photographers, Publishers, and Unidentified Photographers and Publishers.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: The processing archivist and Library staff devised form of names and life dates from the Library of Congress Authorities files or original research.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Arranged alphabetically by the name of the photographer.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of tintypes created 1860-1900 and chiefly collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.

Tintypes, also known as a melainotypes or ferrotypes, are photographs made by creating a direct positive on a thin sheet of metal coated with a dark lacquer or enamel used as the support for a collodion photographic emulsion containing suspended silver halide crystals. Tintypes became widely available during the 1860s and 1870s, however the medium persisted into the early twentieth century. Initially tintype portraits were usually created in a photographic studio, but later itinerant photographers working in booths or the open air at fairs and carnivals as well as on city streets used the format.

The description for this subseries contains 159 entries for discrete images on tintypes, which also includes three examples of duplicate tintypes. The items consist primarily of studio portraiture created by unidentified photographers of unidentified persons.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derive from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Organized under three headings: Images by Identified Photographers, Identified Images by Unidentified Photographers, and Unidentified Images by Unidentified Photographers.

did.unittitle: Cartes-de-visite and Small Mounted Photographic Prints

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries chiefly consists of cartes-de-visite and similarly sized small mounted photographic prints created between 1845 and 1925, with the bulk created between 1860 and 1875, and collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.

Cartes-de-visite represent a photograph format popular in the mid-nineteenth century comprising photographic prints, usually albumen prints made as contact prints from collodion negatives, affixed to card stock. The photographic prints were typically portraits approximately 8.9 x 5.4 cm (3.5 x 2.125 inches) generally produced by multiple-lens camera that created several images on a single full-sized negative plate. The prints were then mounted on cards measuring approximately 10 x 6.4 cm (4 x 2.5 in). The format initially served as visitors' cards. It later became customary to exchange them and collect the cartes-de-visite of friends, family members, and celebrities in albums.

The versos and increasingly rectos of cartes-de-visite carried advertising logos and printing that generally included the photographer's and/or publisher's name and address. Additional notes reminded the public that copies of the carte could be reordered, with pronouncements such as: "Negatives preserved, Duplicates can be had at any time."
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Organized under nine headings: Identified Portraits, Unidentified Portraits by Identified Photographers, Unidentified Portraits by Unidentified Photographers, Composite Images, Animals, Exteriors, Interiors, Artwork, and Still Lifes.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries chiefly consists of cartes-de-visite and similarly sized small mounted photographic prints created between 1845 and 1925, with the bulk created between 1860 and 1875, and collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.

The cartes-de-visite and photographic prints in this subseries chiefly document identified persons principally active in the United States, United Kingdom, and France as well as substantial documentation of persons in Western Europe and Australia. The subjects include military personnel related to the American Civil War of members of the armies and navies of the United States and the Confederate States of America, as well as politicians, theatrical personalities, and clergy members.

The descriptive notes include the Meserve Number applied by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation, in addition to germane biographical information about subjects that provide birthnames, stage names, pseudonyms, and married names, as well as identifying known photographers and publishers of cartes-de-visites and notable physical characteristics or damage.

Portraits of Abraham Lincoln in the subseries also include its Meserve Lincoln Number representing its designation in a numbering system developed by Frederick Hill Meserve as well as its Kunhardt Lincoln Number based on research by Philip B. Kunhardt, Jr. (1928-2006), and refined by James Barber (born 1952), Thomas F. Schwartz, Harold Holzer (born 1949), and Daniel R. Weinberg.

The versos and increasingly rectos of cartes-de-visite carried advertising logos and printing that included the photographer's and/or publisher's name and address. Additional notes reminded the public that copies of the carte could be reordered, with pronouncements such as: "Negatives preserved, Duplicates can be had at any time."
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Arranged alphabetically by surname followed by individuals without known surnames; names appear under 59 headings in this guide, each representing a span of surnames housed in a discrete box.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries chiefly consists of cartes-de-visite and similarly sized small mounted photographic prints created between 1854 and 1898, with the bulk created between 1860 and 1875, and collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.
The cartes-de-visite and photographic prints in this subseries document unidentified persons principally active in the United States created by identified photographers and photographic firms.

The descriptive notes include the Meserve Number applied by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation as well as similar numbers applied during the processing of the collection, as well as identifying known photographers and publishers of cartes-de-visites and notable physical characteristics or damage.

The versos and increasingly rectos of cartes-de-visite carried advertising logos and printing that included the photographer's and/or publisher's name and address. Additional notes reminded the public that copies of the carte could be reordered, with pronouncements such as: "Negatives preserved, Duplicates can be had at any time."
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries chiefly consists of cartes-de-visite with composite photographs in which two or more negatives are printed as a single unified image and created between 1860 and 1881, and collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.

The cartes-de-visite in this subseries chiefly document identified persons principally active in the United States and the United Kingdom, as well as substantial documentation of persons in Western Europe. The subjects include military personnel related to the American Civil War of members of the armies and navies of the United States and the Confederate States of America, as well as politicians, theatrical personalities, chess players, owners of thoroughbred horses, and European royalty.

The descriptive notes include the Meserve Number applied by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation, in addition to germane biographical information about subjects that provide birth names, stage names, pseudonyms, and married names, as well as identifying known photographers and publishers of cartes-de-visites and notable physical characteristics or damage.

The versos and increasingly rectos of cartes-de-visite carried advertising logos and printing that included the photographer's and/or publisher's name and address. Additional notes reminded the public that copies of the carte could be reordered, with pronouncements such as: "Negatives preserved, Duplicates can be had at any time."
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries chiefly consists of cartes-de-visite with images of animals created between 1875 and approximately 1885 and collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.

Photographer Henri-Antoine Boissonnas, 1833-1889, created the bulk of cartes-de-visite in this subseries with images animals in European circuses and zoos and consisting of a leopard, lions, elephants, giraffes, and tigers. Many of the documented animals formed part of the traveling show known as the Menagerie von A. Bach in approximately 1885.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries chiefly consists of cartes-de-visite with images of exterior sites inside and outside the United States created between 1858 and 1900 and collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Organized under two headings: Inside the United States and Outside the United States.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries chiefly consists of cartes-de-visite with images of exterior sites inside the United States created between 1858 and 1886 and collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.
The majority of the carte-de-visites in this subseries document sites during or related to the American Civil War.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

Titles for cartes-de visites created by the processing archivist with the location of the image identified at the beginning of each entry, with each site designated by the state and then the city and/or other geographical point.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Organized under thirteen headings: Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Utah, Virginia, and West Virginia.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of mounted photographs with images of exterior sites outside the United States collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.
The descriptive notes include the Meserve Number applied by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation, identifying known photographers, and notable physical characteristics or damage.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries chiefly consists of cartes-de-visite with copy photographs created between 1860 and 1883 of artwork, including drawings, engravings, paintings, and sculpture, collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries chiefly consists of mounted photographic prints composed chiefly of card photographs, primarily cabinet photographs, as well as photographic prints mounted on leaves from volumes created between 1844 and 1966, with the bulk created between 1860 and 1900 and collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century. The photographs document significant figures, particularly political and military leaders during the American Civil War as well as images of theatrical figures.
Card photographs are commercially produced photographs mounted on thick card stock, usually slightly larger than the image. They were fabricated using various processes with different standard sizes.

Cabinet photographs are card photographs, generally portraits, which generally measure 4.25 by 6.5 inches (approximately 10.8 by 16.5 centimeters), including the mount. They initially appeared in 1867 as larger alternatives to cartes-de-visite, which measure 3.25 by 2.25 inches (approximately 8.25 by 5.75 centimeters). Many photographers and consumers considered the larger size more appropriate for display, allowed for group portraits, and permitted the retouching of images. Cabinet photographs remained popular until the early twentieth century.

The versos and rectos of card photographs often carry advertising logos and printing, which generally include the photographer's and/or publisher's name and address. Additional notes reminded the public that copies of the photograph could be reordered, with pronouncements such as: "Negatives preserved, Duplicates can be had at any time."
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Organized under nine headings: Identified Portraits, Unidentified Portraits by Identified Photographers, Unidentified Portraits by Unidentified Photographers, Composites, Composite Extracts, Exteriors, Interiors, Artwork, and Still Lifes

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The card photographs, cabinet photographs, and mounted photographic prints in this subseries chiefly document identified persons principally active in the United States, United Kingdom, and France as well as substantial documentation of persons in Western Europe and Australia.

The subjects include military personnel related to the American Civil War of members of the armies and navies of the United States and the Confederate States of America, as well as politicians, theatrical personalities, and clergy members. The subseries also includes portraits of prominent and lesser-known boxers posed in fighting stances

The descriptive notes include the Meserve Number applied by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation, in addition to germane biographical information about subjects that provide birthnames, stage names, pseudonyms, and married names, as well as identifying known photographers and publishers of photographs and notable physical characteristics or damage.

Portraits of Abraham Lincoln in the subseries also include its Meserve Lincoln Number representing its designation in a numbering system developed by Frederick Hill Meserve as well as its Kunhardt Lincoln Number based on research by Philip B. Kunhardt, Jr. (1928-2006), and refined by James Barber (born 1952), Thomas F. Schwartz, Harold Holzer (born 1949), and Daniel R. Weinberg.

The versos and increasingly rectos of card photographs carried advertising logos and printing that included the photographer's and/or publisher's name and address. Additional notes reminded the public that copies of the photograph could be reordered, with pronouncements such as: "Negatives preserved, Duplicates can be had at any time."
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Arranged alphabetically by surname followed by individuals without known surnames and oversize photographs.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The card photographs, cabinet photographs, and mounted photographic prints in this subseries chiefly document unidentified persons principally active in the United States, created by identified photographers and photographic firms.

The descriptive notes include the Meserve Number applied by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation as well as similar numbers applied during the processing of the collection, as well as identifying known photographers and publishers of photographs and notable physical characteristics or damage.

The versos and rectos of card photographs carried advertising logos and printing that included the photographer's and/or publisher's name and address. Additional notes reminded the public that copies of the carte could be reordered, with pronouncements such as: "Negatives preserved, Duplicates can be had at any time."
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.p: The card photographs, cabinet photographs, and mounted photographic prints in this subseries chiefly consist of composite photographs in which two or more negatives are printed as a single unified image. The subjects include politicians and theatrical personalities.

The descriptive notes include the Meserve Number applied by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation, in addition to germane biographical information about subjects that provide birth names, stage names, pseudonyms, and married names, as well as identifying known photographers and publishers of photographs and notable physical characteristics or damage.

The versos and rectos of card photographs carried advertising logos and printing that included the photographer's and/or publisher's name and address. Additional notes reminded the public that copies of the carte could be reordered, with pronouncements such as: "Negatives preserved, Duplicates can be had at any time."
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The mounted photographic prints in this subseries consist of portraits of discrete individuals physically cut and extracted from composite photographs, in which two or more negatives are printed as a single unified image. The subjects include politicians that likely attended the funeral of Ulysses S. (Ulysses Simpson) Grant, 1822-1885.
The descriptive notes include the Meserve Number applied by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation, identifying known photographers, and notable physical characteristics or damage.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of mounted photographs with images of exterior sites inside and outside the United States collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.
The descriptive notes include the Meserve Number applied by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation, identifying known photographers, and notable physical characteristics or damage.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Organized under two headings: Inside the United States and Outside the United States.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of mounted photographs with images of exterior sites inside the United States collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.
The majority of the images in this subseries document sites during or related to the American Civil War.
The descriptive notes include the Meserve Number applied by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation, identifying known photographers, and notable physical characteristics or damage.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Organized under seventeen headings: Alabama, Arizona , Colorado, District of Columbia, Georgia, Illinois, Kansas , Maryland, Mississippi, New York, North Carolina , Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Virginia, Washington (State), Unidentified locations, and Oversize.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of mounted photographs with images of exterior sites outside the United States collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century.
The descriptive notes include the Meserve Number applied by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation, identifying known photographers, and notable physical characteristics or damage.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

I. Hood & Company in 1890; rectos of mounted prints damaged with affixed paper remnants; image of Windsor Castle from the River Thames has a printed caption: No. 35 Windsor Castle, England; view of Trafalgar Square includes a fountain and Nelson's Column (1840-1843) and printed caption: No. 32 Nelson's Monument, Trafalgar Square, London; laid-in sheet with halftone is an unnumbered page from John L. (John Lawson) Stoddard, Portfolio of Photographs of Famous Scenes, Cities, and Paintings (Chicago: Educational Pub. Co., 1893) and includes an image of Kenilworth Castle, which documents the ruins of the Great Hall built 1372-1380 by the Duke of Lancaster, John of Gaunt, 1340-1399, as well as an image of the Musée de l'Arc de Triomphe, also known as the Arc de Triomphe de l'Étoile and Arc de Triomphe, which documents the pillars depicting Le Départ de 1792 (1833-1836), also known as La Marseillaise , by François Rude, 1784-1855, and Le Triomphe de 1810 (1833), by Jean-Pierre Cortot, 1787-1843

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries chiefly consists of more than 1750 unmounted photographic prints with images created between 1847 and 1976, with the bulk created between 1860 and 1900 and collected by Frederick Hill Meserve and Dorothy Meserve Kunhardt during the twentieth century. The content provides rich visual documentation of the history of the United States, especially the American Civil War.

Unlike card photographs, such as cartes-de-visite and cabinet cards, which circulated widely in mounted formats, these prints were preserved without their original mounts, providing a more direct look at the material qualities of the photographs themselves. The subseries includes both albumen prints made directly from negatives and later copy photographs. Many of the copy photographs date to approximately 1885, reflecting the period of intensive collecting and reproduction projects related to the American Civil War. Several prints originated from negatives held by Brady's National Photographic Portrait Galleries.
The photographs primarily document two major areas: nineteenth-century military and political leaders and the twentieth-century theatrical and film industry.

The core of the subseries documents significant figures, particularly political and military leaders during the American Civil War, with portraits of generals, officers, and politicians. The subseries also features extensive material documenting figures and sites related to Universal City, California, and Universal Pictures. These prints frequently showcase actors, producers, and sets related to silent films. Later content, dating up to 1976, frequently consists of copy photographs related to the collection's history and photography itself, often created for Time-Life Books.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Organized under two headings: Smaller than 11 x 13 centimeters and Larger than 11 x 13 centimeters.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The material in this subseries measures smaller than 11 x 13 centimeters.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Organized under five headings: Identified Portraits, Exteriors in the United States, Interiors, Artwork, and Still Lifes.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists primarily of small, unmounted photographic prints documenting identified individuals. The photographs generally measure smaller than 11 x 13 centimeters, providing a clear view of the material qualities of the prints, which are preserved without their original card mounts.

The photographs overwhelmingly feature portraits of significant figures, particularly those related to the history of the United States, with a strong emphasis on political and military leaders of the American Civil War.
Key subjects represented by these small portraits include prominent United States Army generals and officers, well as Confederate States of America officers, as well as political figures and actors.

While many of the original images date from periods between 1861 and 1865, the majority of the items in this subseries are copy photographs generally created approximately 1885, reflecting a period when entities were engaged in intensive collecting and reproduction projects related to the American Civil War.
Many portraits originated from the collections of Brady's National Photographic Portrait Galleries.

The descriptive notes attached to the individual items in this subseries were derived primarily from documentation provided by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and subsequently reviewed by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of unmounted photographic prints, measuring smaller than 11 x 13 centimeters, documenting locations and structures within the United States.

The subject matter overwhelmingly focuses on sites and events related to the American Civil War. Primary subjects include military camps, fortifications, and infrastructure, as well as battlefield views and aftermath, in addition to buildings and civilian sites of historical significance.

This subseries chiefly includes images created between 1861 and 1865. A substantial number of these are later copy photographs, often dating to approximately 1885, during a period of intensive Civil War reproduction projects. A key production characteristic is that many items are details reproduced from stereographic negatives. Several original images were captured by well-known Civil War photographers and studios.

The descriptive notes attached to the individual items in this subseries were derived primarily from documentation provided by the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and subsequently reviewed by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries primarily consists of unmounted photographic prints documenting identified individuals. The photographs generally measure larger than 11 x 13 centimeters, providing a clear view of the material qualities of the prints, which are preserved without their original card mounts.

The photographs overwhelmingly feature portraits of significant figures, particularly those related to the history of the United States, with a strong emphasis on political and military leaders of the American Civil War and twentieth-century theatrical and film figures.

Key subjects of the American Civil War represented by these portraits include prominent United States Army generals and officers, Confederate States of America officers, political figures, and actors. While many of the original images date from periods between 1861 and 1865, most of the items in this subseries are copy photographs generally created approximately 1885, reflecting a period when entities were engaged in intensive collecting and reproduction projects related to the American Civil War. Many portraits originated from the collections of Brady's National Photographic Portrait Galleries.

Twentieth-century theatrical and film documentation includes portraits of theatrical figures, many of which relate to Universal City, California, and Universal Pictures, frequently featuring actors, producers, and sets related to silent films.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Arranged alphabetically, followed by unidentified portraits, also arranged alphabetically, and then identified portraits on oversized prints, also arranged alphabetically.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of unmounted photographic prints that document sites, architecture, and historical events across the United States.

The images chiefly document American Civil War and historic sites, especially related to military installations and naval vessels, military campaigns in Virginia, and sites associated with Abaraham Lincoln, as well as silent film production and Universal City, California during the early twentieth-century including studio buildings and sets, actors and personnel, and events.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Arranged alphabetically, followed by unidentified exteriors, also arranged alphabetically, and then exteriors on oversized prints.

scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of photographic prints documenting subjects from numerous international locations, focusing on areas affected by early twentieth-century geopolitical conflicts and sites of historical or cultural significance.

The materials cover diverse geographies and historical themes, including the Mexican Revolution and United States Border Conflict, approximately 1914-1916, as well as global political and cultural figures, such as Charles Dickens and Kai-shek Chiang.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of unmounted photographic prints documenting interior scenes in the United States.

The content generally falls into two major chronological and thematic groups: extensive documentation of the early twentieth-century silent film industry in California and later photography documenting Abraham Lincoln, Civil War history, and relics.

The bulk of the material documents the operations of Universal Pictures at Universal City, California, focusing heavily on actors, producers, and fabricated sets used in silent film production. These prints often include detailed identification of subjects and technical information, often via typescript descriptions affixed to the versos. Key individuals and scenes documented include actors and actresses, production and studio life, visitors, and dignitaries.

A sizable portion of prints documents preserved historical settings and relics, particularly related to the life and death of Abraham Lincoln, including relics and artifacts as well as historical locations.
Other prints document historical figures in non-film settings, such as a boxing bout for the Heavyweight Championship of the World at Madison Square Garden in New York City.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

Brady, approximately 1823-1896, and used for portraits at Brady's National Photographic Portrait Galleries, and the chair transferred with sale of the studio to William H. Stalee, 1865-1900, in 1893, and his widow, Helen M. Ayres Stalee Wenger, 1866-1930, sold it to Will H. (William Henry) Towles in 1903, and inerited by his daughter Thelma E Towles Pattison, 1899-1980, also known as Mrs. William Hoffman Pattison, and it remained in the Pattison family until its sale as Lot 1215 in the Fine Furniture, Silver, Decorative Arts and Clocks sale at Bonhams New York, October 26, 2015

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of unmounted photographic prints documenting interior scenes located outside the United States.

The chiefly copy photographs concentrate on high-profile British and international social and political figures and events around the turn of the twentieth century, typically related to conflict, diplomacy and society. It includes South African (Second Boer) War documentation and British political and social events.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.p: Meserve Number MES33655; copy photograph; image documents a farewell dinner on the appointment of the Marquess Curzon of Kedleston as the viceroy and governor-general of India, commonly shortened to viceroy of India; the image documents approximately 40-50 attendees posed sitting at tables and two male waitstaff posed standing; Lady Mary Curzon was born Mary Victoria Leiter and also known as Mary Victoria Curzon, Baroness Curzon of Kedleston, and Mrs. George Nathaniel Curzon; the Marquess Curzon of Kedleston and is posed sitting closest to the camera with Lady Curzon to the right of him and next closest to the camera; image created by Fradelle & Young, operated by Albert Young, 1865-1834; photographic print created by William E. Gray, 1864-1935

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of unmounted photographic prints that focus entirely on documenting artwork. The artwork primarily depicts historical figures and events, with an overwhelming emphasis on Abraham Lincoln and subjects related to the American Civil War. The items are largely copy photographs of sculptures, maquettes, paintings, sketches, and bas-reliefs.
A substantial portion of this subseries documents various artistic interpretations and studies of Abraham Lincoln by twentieth-century sculptors, as well as sculptures of other subjects.
The subseries contains copy photographs of paintings and sketches, primarily related to military scenes and nineteenth-century figures, as well as other artwork.
Several copy prints of historical drawings bear an ink stamp for The Century Company, reflecting the possible use of these images for publication in Century Magazine .
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This subseries consists of unmounted photographic prints documenting scenes, characters, and publicity related to silent film production, predominantly from approximately 1914 to 1918, and chiefly related to Universal City, California, and Universal Pictures. It frequently features actors, producers, and sets related to silent films.
The stills primarily fall into two categories: identified films and unidentified productions.

The largest concentration of material documents major silent films and features work from notable directors and stars of the era. The subseries also includes multiple sets of stills from unnamed productions documenting various genres.
The descriptive notes associated with individual items primarily derived from documentation received from the Meserve-Kunhardt Foundation and examination of the material by the processing archivist.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series includes cultural artifacts and realia chiefly collected by Frederick Hill Meserve, approximately 1897 to 1962, and supplemented by the collecting efforts of his daughter, Dorothy Turner Meserve Kunhardt.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Series II currently consists of one subseries: Negative Boxes.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Wooden boxes with hinged lids created approximately 1870 that previously held glass negatives produced by Brady's National Photographic Portrait Galleries. The 26 boxes were likely sent to the E. and H.T. Anthony photographic supply company filled with negatives created by the firm to distrubte under its imprint or as payment for debt following the American Civil War. The boxes, of varying sizes, include slots to accommodate glass plates as small as 9.5 x 16 cm (3.5 x 6.25 inches) to as large as 16.5 x 19.5 cm (6.5 x 7.75 inches). Painted inscriptions on each box appear to describe briefly the negatives they originally contained. This guide uses the painted inscriptions as titles for the boxes. Given discontinuities in the inscriptions it seems possible that the 26 boxes gathered here are an incomplete survival of the original shipment.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: Arranged alphabetically by painted inscriptions on boxes.
